terms.context: A single note the user adds to or edits on a block
A paragraph, list item, heading, etc. in the document that a note attaches to
terms.notes: Transliterated from English rather than translated (e.g. not פסקה, which is reserved for 'paragraph' specifically)

terms.context: The panel listing every note in the file; section heading "The notes list"
Bar at the bottom of the window showing confirmation messages like "Note added"
Bar at the top of the window holding File, Edit, View, Notes, Help
terms.notes: Definite form שורת התפריטים is used when referring back to it (e.g. reaching it with Alt); the indefinite שורת תפריטים appears once, on first mention of the window layout

terms.context: The note markers, e.g. [usernote]/[/usernote]; "changing the markers" warning
A Markdown checklist item; "Mark this task as done?" confirmation and "Checking off tasks" section
The "Document language" setting and View-menu submenu name
terms.notes: Indefinite form שפת מסמך is the setting/menu item label; the general concept and section heading "The document's language" use the definite form שפת המסמך

terms.context: The "Interface language" setting and View-menu submenu name
terms.notes: Indefinite form שפת ממשק is the setting/menu item label; running prose referring to "the interface language" uses the definite form שפת הממשק

terms.context: Generic word for a dialog box, e.g. the Open dialog or a confirmation dialog
The two buttons on a yes-or-no confirmation, e.g. "Mark this task as done?"
Windows Explorer, e.g. dragging a file from it or its "Copy as path" command
The Windows Downloads folder where files opened from a link are saved
Starting PlanCake from the Windows Start menu
terms.notes: "Start" is kept in Latin script, hyphen-joined to the Hebrew prefix ה-

terms.context: Windows Command Prompt, as contrasted with PowerShell
File Explorer's "Copy as path" command, which adds quotation marks around the copied path
A GitHub issue, "Paste them into a new issue on PlanCake's GitHub page"
terms.notes: The manual keeps the English word "issue" in parentheses next to the Hebrew תקלה for clarity, since תקלה alone reads as "malfunction/fault"

terms.context: GitHub's "Raw" link for viewing/downloading a file's plain contents
